title: One compiled round reaches its live exit
statement: Let $M$ be a $k$-work-tape binary machine with states indexed by $	ext{Fin}(n+1)$, and let $c$ and $d$ be configurations such that $d$ starts at the live exit anchor and represents $c$. For a natural number $r$, suppose the simulated machine has a present state at every time $u ullet ullet ullet r$. Let $e$ be the configuration after iterating the compiled machine for $r$ exit-delimited rounds. Then $e$ is again at the live exit anchor, and the duration of the next round is positive and at most $50(|\text{tableBits}(M)|+1)$. At every strictly intermediate time in that round, the compiled machine is in a state different from both exit anchors.
hypotheses_covered: Natural numbers $k,n$ and binary input list $x$
$d$ starts at the live exit anchor
Machine remains running at every time $u\le r$
